## Motivation

- On ROCm, Kimi-K3 has a fused KDA decode kernel: `f_b` projection + convolution + recurrent update + gated RMSNorm in one gfx950 launch per KDA layer.
- With the `aiter` backend it never turns on for the deployed Quark checkpoint (`amd/Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`), so decode silently runs the unfused chain and pays the extra launches every step:

| Blocker | Cause |
|---|---|
| Wrong AITER module | `SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE=aiter` imports a module no AITER build ships; ROCm/aiter#6026 publishes the kernel under another name |
| BF16 recurrent state rejected | the adapter accepts FP32 only, but the recommended `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` pool is BF16 |
| FP8 `f_b` | the checkpoint stores `f_b` as per-channel FP8; the kernel takes dense BF16 |

- The two fused-decode env vars were read with raw `os.environ`, outside `Envs`.

## Modifications

- Bind `flydsl_kda_decode_with_f_b` from `aiter.ops.flydsl.linear_attention_kernels`; if AITER lacks ROCm/aiter#6026, warn once and fall back.
- Arm a fused kernel only if it takes the pool's state dtype (the AITER op advertises `state_dtypes`); otherwise warn once and keep the unfused path.
- Dequantize the Quark per-channel FP8 `f_b` to a BF16 copy once, for the fused kernel only; the FP8 layer keeps serving the unfused path.
- Mirror AITER's cache-slot and stride rules in `covered()`, so an unsupported layout falls back instead of raising.
- Warm up only the pool's state dtype before graph capture; log the armed kernel and dtype.
- Apply the deferred `f_b` on the ReplaySSM decode-ring path too (it has no fused kernel); before, that path received the raw `f_a`.
- Scope: ROCm only. CUDA is unchanged.

Arming rules:

| Backend | State dtype | Other conditions | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gfx950` (default) | FP32 | gfx950 | armed |
| `gfx950` | BF16 | - | not armed, one-time warning |
| `aiter`, source `auto` / `sglang` (vendored kernel) | FP32 | gfx950 | armed |
| `aiter`, source `auto` / `sglang` | BF16 | - | not armed, one-time warning |
| `aiter`, source `aiter` | FP32 or BF16 | AITER with ROCm/aiter#6026 | armed |
| `aiter`, source `aiter` | any | AITER without #6026 | not armed, one-time warning |
| any | any | Quark `f_b` already post-processed (`ShardedStateLoader`, `RemoteModelLoader`) | not armed, one-time warning |

Env vars (moved into `Envs`; the old names keep working with a `DeprecationWarning`):

| Name | Deprecated alias | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SGLANG_USE_HIP_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND` | `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND` | `gfx950` | `gfx950`: SGLang HIP kernel; `aiter`: FlyDSL boundary; other values: unfused decode |
| `SGLANG_USE_HIP_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE` | `SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE` | `auto` | FlyDSL module behind `aiter`: `auto` prefers the vendored copy, `sglang` / `aiter` pin one |

- Docs: both vars in the AMD & ROCm env-var table; the Kimi-K3 cookbook documents the FP8 dequant and the state-dtype rule (it keeps the old names for its pinned image).

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, [sgl-eval](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-eval) 0.1.3, `--load-preset-from-model-id moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking on), all 1319 questions, one run per side.

| `main` | This PR (fused KDA decode on) |
|---:|---:|
| 97.27% | 97.12% |

- The 0.15-point gap is 2 questions, within noise (standard error about +/-0.45 points).

Unit and kernel tests (one MI355X):

| Test | AITER | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `test_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py` | integration build with ROCm/aiter#6026 (`6ae4bf0f2`) | 25 passed |
| `test_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py` | pinned image `285579b62` (no #6026) | 15 passed, 10 skipped |
| `test_kda_fused_decode_gfx950.py` | pinned image | 4 passed |
| `test_kimi_k3_rocm_quant.py` | CPU | 8 passed |

- Latest head: the three files pass together (39 passed) on MI355X with the ROCm/aiter stack at `f9b5308b2` (has #6026).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Setup: 8x MI355X, TP8, random 8192 in / 1024 out, radix cache off, FP8 KV, AITER attention, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`.
- Base: `main` at `dd9ea06c00`. PR side adds `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE=aiter`.
- AITER `be461934f` (has ROCm/aiter#6026) on both sides. One run per side; a repeat of `main` matched its TPOT within 0.4%.

| Conc | TPOT base (ms) | TPOT PR (ms) | Delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 18.22 | 17.70 | -2.9% |
| 4 | 19.90 | 19.31 | -2.9% |
| 8 | 23.00 | 22.48 | -2.3% |
| 16 | 28.12 | 27.51 | -2.2% |
| 32 | 36.64 | 36.33 | -0.8% (noise) |
| 64 | 52.85 | 52.35 | -0.9% (noise) |

- TPOT drops 2.2-2.9% at concurrency 2-16; at 32 and 64 the change is about twice the noise, so it is not claimed.
- TTFT does not change (within +/-0.8%), as expected for a decode-only change.
- These numbers come from an earlier revision; later changes touch load-time checks, warnings, warm-up and the ReplaySSM fallback, not the kernels.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

detail.body:
## Motivation

- On ROCm, Kimi-K3 has a fused KDA decode kernel: `f_b` projection + convolution + recurrent update + gated RMSNorm in one gfx950 launch per KDA layer.
- With the `aiter` backend it never turns on for the deployed Quark checkpoint (`amd/Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`), so decode silently runs the unfused chain and pays the extra launches every step:

| Blocker | Cause |
|---|---|
| Wrong AITER module | `SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE=aiter` imports a module no AITER build ships; ROCm/aiter#6026 publishes the kernel under another name |
| BF16 recurrent state rejected | the adapter accepts FP32 only, but the recommended `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16` pool is BF16 |
| FP8 `f_b` | the checkpoint stores `f_b` as per-channel FP8; the kernel takes dense BF16 |

- The two fused-decode env vars were read with raw `os.environ`, outside `Envs`.

## Modifications

- Bind `flydsl_kda_decode_with_f_b` from `aiter.ops.flydsl.linear_attention_kernels`; if AITER lacks ROCm/aiter#6026, warn once and fall back.
- Arm a fused kernel only if it takes the pool's state dtype (the AITER op advertises `state_dtypes`); otherwise warn once and keep the unfused path.
- Dequantize the Quark per-channel FP8 `f_b` to a BF16 copy once, for the fused kernel only; the FP8 layer keeps serving the unfused path.
- Mirror AITER's cache-slot and stride rules in `covered()`, so an unsupported layout falls back instead of raising.
- Warm up only the pool's state dtype before graph capture; log the armed kernel and dtype.
- Apply the deferred `f_b` on the ReplaySSM decode-ring path too (it has no fused kernel); before, that path received the raw `f_a`.
- Scope: ROCm only. CUDA is unchanged.

Arming rules:

| Backend | State dtype | Other conditions | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gfx950` (default) | FP32 | gfx950 | armed |
| `gfx950` | BF16 | - | not armed, one-time warning |
| `aiter`, source `auto` / `sglang` (vendored kernel) | FP32 | gfx950 | armed |
| `aiter`, source `auto` / `sglang` | BF16 | - | not armed, one-time warning |
| `aiter`, source `aiter` | FP32 or BF16 | AITER with ROCm/aiter#6026 | armed |
| `aiter`, source `aiter` | any | AITER without #6026 | not armed, one-time warning |
| any | any | Quark `f_b` already post-processed (`ShardedStateLoader`, `RemoteModelLoader`) | not armed, one-time warning |

Env vars (moved into `Envs`; the old names keep working with a `DeprecationWarning`):

| Name | Deprecated alias | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SGLANG_USE_HIP_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND` | `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND` | `gfx950` | `gfx950`: SGLang HIP kernel; `aiter`: FlyDSL boundary; other values: unfused decode |
| `SGLANG_USE_HIP_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE` | `SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE` | `auto` | FlyDSL module behind `aiter`: `auto` prefers the vendored copy, `sglang` / `aiter` pin one |

- Docs: both vars in the AMD & ROCm env-var table; the Kimi-K3 cookbook documents the FP8 dequant and the state-dtype rule (it keeps the old names for its pinned image).

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, [sgl-eval](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-eval) 0.1.3, `--load-preset-from-model-id moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking on), all 1319 questions, one run per side.

| `main` | This PR (fused KDA decode on) |
|---:|---:|
| 97.27% | 97.12% |

- The 0.15-point gap is 2 questions, within noise (standard error about +/-0.45 points).

Unit and kernel tests (one MI355X):

| Test | AITER | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `test_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py` | integration build with ROCm/aiter#6026 (`6ae4bf0f2`) | 25 passed |
| `test_kimi_k3_kda_decode.py` | pinned image `285579b62` (no #6026) | 15 passed, 10 skipped |
| `test_kda_fused_decode_gfx950.py` | pinned image | 4 passed |
| `test_kimi_k3_rocm_quant.py` | CPU | 8 passed |

- Latest head: the three files pass together (39 passed) on MI355X with the ROCm/aiter stack at `f9b5308b2` (has #6026).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Setup: 8x MI355X, TP8, random 8192 in / 1024 out, radix cache off, FP8 KV, AITER attention, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`.
- Base: `main` at `dd9ea06c00`. PR side adds `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_KDA_FUSED_BACKEND=aiter SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_SOURCE=aiter`.
- AITER `be461934f` (has ROCm/aiter#6026) on both sides. One run per side; a repeat of `main` matched its TPOT within 0.4%.

| Conc | TPOT base (ms) | TPOT PR (ms) | Delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 18.22 | 17.70 | -2.9% |
| 4 | 19.90 | 19.31 | -2.9% |
| 8 | 23.00 | 22.48 | -2.3% |
| 16 | 28.12 | 27.51 | -2.2% |
| 32 | 36.64 | 36.33 | -0.8% (noise) |
| 64 | 52.85 | 52.35 | -0.9% (noise) |

- TPOT drops 2.2-2.9% at concurrency 2-16; at 32 and 64 the change is about twice the noise, so it is not claimed.
- TTFT does not change (within +/-0.8%), as expected for a decode-only change.
- These numbers come from an earlier revision; later changes touch load-time checks, warnings, warm-up and the ReplaySSM fallback, not the kernels.
